title: Advanced silencer geometry and alcohol‐diesel fuel blends: A CFD study on emissions and exhaust characteristic for sustainable environment
content:
Abstract

The use of alcohol-diesel blends offers a potential pathway to reduce carbon-based emissions in internal combustion engines. However, these blends can increase exhaust temperatures and NO x emissions, necessitating efficient exhaust system designs. This study investigates the effect of silencer geometry and fuel blending on diesel engine exhaust characteristics using computational fluid dynamics (CFD). Four muffler designs—non-perforated turbo straight (NPTS), non-perforated turbo elliptical (NPTE), perforated turbo straight (PTS), and perforated turbo elliptical (PTE)—were analyzed with varying blends of diesel and octanol (Oct 10 and Oct 20). Results show that the NPTE muffler with Oct 20 fuel produced the highest back pressure of 2.392 Pa and maximum exhaust temperature of 368.4 K. In contrast, the PTE muffler with diesel showed the lowest back pressure of 0.8055 Pa due to its multiple expansion paths. The highest gas density, 1.7304 kg/m3, was observed for the PTE muffler with Oct 20, while non-perforated types had minimum values around 1.16 kg/m3. The maximum exhaust velocity, 1.091 m/s, was recorded for the PTS muffler with Oct 20. These findings highlight the importance of muffler design in optimizing performance for sustainable fuel use.
